1: Impulse is the force times the time it acts, and it equals the change in momentum. Momentum is a vector, so in two dimensions each component is conserved separately.
2: An elastic collision conserves kinetic energy, while an inelastic collision transfers some of it to other forms. You decide which by comparing the kinetic energy before and after.
3: Kinetic energy is ½mv², and substituting p = mv gives p²/(2m). Expressing it in momentum is useful when momentum is conserved.
4: Angles in radians make arc length s = rθ and the link v = rω direct. Angular velocity is the angle turned per unit time, so it is the rotational analogue of linear speed.
5: A body moving in a circle changes direction, so its velocity changes and it accelerates towards the centre. The resultant force towards the centre is what provides this acceleration, F = mv²/r.
